newsitem.title: UK: IPE gas oil ends firm led by NYMEX heating oil.
newsitem.headline: IPE gas oil ends firm led by NYMEX heating oil.

text.p: IPE gas oil futures ended firmer as short-covering following Tuesday's U.S. stock draw strengthened NYMEX heating oil, traders said.
The March gas oil contract last traded $2 firmer at $184.75 a tonne.
The February contract expired at noon 50 cents off at $192 with a physical delivery of 558,500 tonnes.
Traders believed most of the lots to be delivered were in the hands of two key players.
"I think a lot of is already placed. I'm hearing freight has already been fixed by these guys," said one trader.
U.S. traders were quick to point out the gains on heating oil were mainly as a result of short covering and there was no new buying.

Though many were heartened by the apparent growth in distillate demand which saw a fall of 4.9 million barrels in U.S. distillate stocks last week most expected a reversal of the gains "once the shorts are covered".
"It's too late in the season for the heating oil to keep leading the market and not early enough for the gasoline to take over," one traders said.
After dipping around 30 cents to new lows in the hour before the NYMEX market opened March Brent futures were trading four cents up at $21.18 a barrel, near the day's high, at the close of gas oil.
